source: Prince William County Development Services ePortal (Tyler EnerGov SelfService), permit search API (POST /SelfService/api/energov/search/search, EnableDescriptionSearch=true)
method: Reverse-engineered the ePortal search API (tenant headers tenantId=3/PWCePortal). Swept ~2,900 permits across keywords {data center, critical load, megawatt, data server vault, MVA} with description-search enabled; regex-extracted MW/vault statements; required 'data center' context and excluded solar/PV (one 20 MW ENERGIX solar farm was a false positive and is excluded).
finding: Stated electrical/critical load appears in the permit descriptions of only 5 data-center parcels county-wide -- disclosure of load is sparse, consistent with the project's transparency-gap thesis. Stated values are CRITICAL (design IT) load; effective demand ~= critical x 0.8 utilization (ICPRB Eq 6-3).

validation.verdict: CONSISTENT within the fitted +/-28% band (validates the fitted model)
COLLISION: 2025 new-structure permit shares an address with an older modeled building (in_model=false in density_statements); NOT a correction
AMBIGUOUS: parcel touches multiple buildings; not cleanly attributable

conclusion: Stated critical load is disclosed for only 5 data-center parcels county-wide. Where it cleanly maps to a modeled building it CORROBORATES the power spine (NTT, Stack) rather than correcting it; the discrepant cases are permit-vs-GIS-inventory address collisions, not model errors. Tier 2 of the evidence ladder is therefore left empty rather than populated with unreliable overwrites: the sweep's value is a second independent validation of power (after the JLARC Scope-1 distributional test), plus two data-completeness findings.
